name: TOMUS
question: Are retropubic and transobturator midurethral slings equivalent for objective and subjective treatment success in women with stress-predominant urinary incontinence?

design.blinding: Open-label after surgery; surgeons masked to preoperative urodynamic results
design.population: Women aged at least 21 years with at least 3 months of stress-predominant incontinence and a positive stress test at bladder volume 300 mL or less; 597 randomized at 9 US sites.

verdictNote: Objective 12-month equivalence met; subjective equivalence did not.
takeaway: Retropubic TVT and transobturator TVT-O or Monarc had equivalent objective success at 12 months (80.8% versus 77.7%) under TOMUS's ±12-point margin; subjective success (62.2% versus 55.8%) did not meet equivalence. Complication patterns differed by route.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Richter HE, Albo ME, Zyczynski HM, et al. "Retropubic versus Transobturator Midurethral Slings for Stress Incontinence." *N Engl J Med.* 2010;362(22):2066-2076. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa0912658
reports.followUp: 12 months; 565/597 assessed or counted as failures

results.measure: 12-month objective composite; retropubic minus transobturator risk difference, percentage points
results.note: Negative provocative stress test, negative 24-hour pad test, and no SUI retreatment; full 95% CI within ±12 points.

results.measure: 12-month subjective composite; retropubic minus transobturator risk difference, percentage points
results.note: No stress symptoms on MESA, no leakage in 3-day diary, and no SUI retreatment; upper CI exceeded +12 points.

harms.label: Intraoperative bladder perforation
harms.note: Trocar perforations were managed by replacement of the trocar.

harms.label: Voiding dysfunction requiring surgery by 12 months
Neurologic symptoms assessed through 6 weeks
harms.note: Leg weakness and groin numbness were among symptoms reported.

delivery.label: Operative routes and devices
delivery.value: Retropubic Gynecare TVT versus inside-out Gynecare TVT-O or outside-in AMS Monarc; surgeons declared their transobturator method before enrollment; cystoscopy and key elements standardized; concomitant vaginal surgery permitted.

delivery.label: Transobturator approach used
delivery.value: Inside-out in 161 women and outside-in in 137; one assigned transobturator patient received a retropubic sling.

reports.label: Two-year adverse events
reports.dateLocator: PubMed issue date; exact online date not confirmed
reports.citation: Brubaker L, Norton PA, Albo ME, et al. "Adverse Events over Two Years after Retropubic or Transobturator Midurethral Sling Surgery: Findings from the Trial of Midurethral Slings (TOMUS) Study." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;205(5):498.e1-498.e6. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2011.07.011

harms.label: At least one serious adverse event through 24 months
harms.note: Modified Dindo classification; an intraoperative perforation requiring trocar replacement counted as serious.

harms.label: Voiding dysfunction requiring surgery, catheter use, or both through 24 months
Vaginal mesh exposure through 24 months
harms.locator: Table 1, serious and nonserious exposure rows combined
harms.note: Patients with exposure; excludes one erosion into an organ in each arm.

harms.label: Neurologic adverse event through 24 months
harms.note: Four neurologic symptoms remained unresolved at 24 months across both arms.

reports.label: 24-month efficacy
reports.citation: Albo ME, Litman HJ, Richter HE, et al. "Treatment Success of Retropubic and Transobturator Mid Urethral Slings at 24 Months." *J Urol.* 2012;188(6):2281-2287. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.07.103
reports.followUp: 24 months; 516/597 (86.4%) assessed or counted as failures

results.measure: 24-month objective composite; retropubic minus transobturator risk difference, percentage points
results.note: Upper 95% CI exceeded the prespecified +12-point equivalence boundary.

results.measure: 24-month subjective composite; retropubic minus transobturator risk difference, percentage points
results.note: Upper 95% CI exceeded the prespecified +12-point equivalence boundary.

reports.label: Five-year observational follow-up
reports.citation: Kenton K, Stoddard AM, Zyczynski H, et al. "5-Year Longitudinal Followup after Retropubic and Transobturator Mid Urethral Slings." *J Urol.* 2015;193(1):203-210. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2014.08.089

results.measure: Five-year cohort success without SUI symptoms or retreatment; retropubic minus transobturator risk difference, percentage points
results.note: Different success definition from the original composites; CI crossed zero and exceeded the cohort's prespecified ±15-point equivalence margin.

harms.label: New mesh findings during extended follow-up
harms.note: Seven new mesh findings were reported across the two arms; terminology varies between erosion and exposure.

delivery.label: Extended follow-up enrollment and analysis
delivery.value: 404/597 (68%) of the original randomized women enrolled; original trial completers without surgical retreatment were invited; time-to-failure analysis included 583 per-protocol operated women.
